anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
**(1) First message**

```text
gauntlet: question
Before the first question, here is what checked out. Completed runs persist a completion date, and the latest succeeded run is ordered by completion date descending, then id descending (svc-a/run-store.md). Rendering reads persisted data and never calls svc-b (svc-b/response-contract.md), so the persisted-data constraint holds. The draft says every completed run persists the svc-b revision, but that is wrong: the producer version is optional on a run, and a missing one displays as "unknown version" (svc-a/run-store.md). The draft also says svc-a's release identity is absent from run metadata. That is wrong for new runs, because successful completion already stores svc-a's release identity on the run (svc-a/run-store.md), so persisting it is existing behavior, not new work. Whether historical runs lack it is unverified, since no fixture shows historical rows or a backfill. I am assuming older runs may have none. The release tag displays only when the svc-a revision matches the producer revision (svc-a/run-store.md). The draft's join claims hold. Placement provenance selects the latest succeeded run for (file, destination) and never borrows another placement's run (svc-a/file-chip.md). The root item badge uses the latest succeeded run touching the root or its descendants via candidates (svc-a/workspace.md). I am also assuming no child-item badges and no provenance stamped on files or items, as svc-a/workspace.md states.

For the framing, I traced the shared hover renderer behind file-chip, run selection and ordering in run-store, the placement provenance join, the root/descendant candidate join, and the svc-b read-only contract. The draft's concern holds. A workspace's latest run does not establish any one file's or item's provenance. The ask's revision-only hover also omits the date that the binding outcome requires.
A) as framed - a revision-only file hover plus a badge on each top-level item
B) pivot: three surfaces, each labeled by its own run - the document card shows the workspace's latest succeeded run date and version, the file tooltip uses placement provenance, and the root item badge uses the last run touching the root or its descendants, each showing date and version from that one run (svc-a/workspace.md, svc-a/file-chip.md)
C) smaller or none: document card only - the workspace date with the producer revision reachable from its hover meets the binding outcome, with no per-file or per-item indicator
Recommendation: B - every surface shows the run that actually produced what it labels, and the existing joins already supply those runs.
```

**(2) Approaches message** (after the recorded answers: all three surfaces, release tag when available, persist release identity on the run, derive provenance at read time, the root uses the last touch on it or its descendants, quiet badges with browser-local date-time)

```text
gauntlet: question
Three dependencies are missing or not checkable:

- **Producer version.** It is optional on a run (svc-a/run-store.md). Runs without one render "unknown version" and are never hidden.
- **Historical release identity.** It cannot be checked. svc-a/run-store.md shows successful completion storing it, but no fixture shows historical rows or a backfill. Older runs get no tag and fall back to the producer revision, which matches your answer.
- **Release tag gating.** Your answer assumed the services deploy together. That premise is corrected by code: the tag displays only when the svc-a revision matches the producer revision (svc-a/run-store.md). A mismatched run shows the producer revision alone.

Your replies settled every assumption in the ask: the surfaces, revision-only display, and stamping. So there is no remaining assumption to drop. Stamping provenance on items is not viable either: svc-a/workspace.md forbids it, and you chose read-time joins. The approaches differ on one axis: where run selection lives.

**Recommended: reuse-only, per-surface selection on existing paths.** Each surface reads its run through the selector that already owns it:
- The document card uses run-store's workspace-wide latest succeeded run.
- The file tooltip uses file-chip's placement provenance.
- The root badge uses the latest succeeded run touching the root or its descendants via candidates.

All three go through the shared hover renderer, given an optional field set: browser-local date-time, producer version or "unknown version", and the gated release tag. Badges are quiet and spaced. The renderer has other callers (file-chip), so the new fields must stay optional to keep that blast radius at zero.

Removes: none
Adds: optional date/version/release-tag parameter on the shared hover renderer; root-or-descendants scope on the latest-succeeded-run selector; document-card, file-tooltip, and root-badge call sites; browser-local date-time formatting at render; tests for each surface, the unknown-version case, and the tag-mismatch case
Pattern: follows svc-a/file-chip.md (shared hover renderer, placement provenance) and svc-a/run-store.md (persisted completion metadata, single ordering rule)

**Alternative: a central read-time provenance resolver.** A new module answers "which run labels this thing?" for workspace, placement, and root. The three surfaces call it, and placement selection moves into it out of file-chip. This gives one call site for future surfaces and batched root lookups. The cost is a second owner of run selection beside run-store's ordering.

Removes: placement-provenance selection inline in file-chip (moved)
Adds: ProvenanceResolver module and its result type; three resolver methods; rewired file-chip, document-card, and root-badge call sites; resolver tests
Pattern: cuts across svc-a/run-store.md, which already owns latest-succeeded-run ordering, so it creates a parallel selection path

The flip condition: if root badges render in bulk and per-root queries become an N+1 problem, or a fourth surface lands, the central resolver wins.
A) reuse-only per-surface selection
B) central provenance resolver
Recommendation: A - the existing selectors already return the right run for each surface, and nothing new owns provenance.
```

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
### 1. First message to the user

The framing holds as an assessment of the existing three surfaces: the supplied fixtures describe workspace-run selection, placement-specific file provenance, root-and-descendant provenance, persisted completion metadata, and rendering without svc-b calls. They already describe the requested behavior, so I would assess those paths before proposing new implementation.

One premise needs tightening: deploying the services together does not establish matching revisions. `svc-a/run-store.md` permits a release tag **only when svc-a’s revision matches the producer revision**. “When available” therefore means available **and demonstrably matching**; otherwise, show the persisted producer revision, or “unknown version” when that is missing.

Your recorded decisions establish the presentation and scope: retain the document card, file tooltip, and root-only badge; use quiet styling with proper spacing and browser-local date-time alongside the version; persist release identity on successful completion; and derive provenance through existing joins without syncing or stamping files or items.

The binding workspace indicator uses the latest succeeded run’s completion date and that same run’s version. A file tooltip instead selects the latest succeeded run for its exact `(file, destination)` placement, never another placement. A root badge selects the latest succeeded run touching that root or its descendants through candidates. The documented ordering is completion date descending, then ID descending.

The fixtures support those rules, but do not supply executable implementations, tests, or the fields used to prove revision equality. Those remain verification gaps—not evidence that the behavior is absent. Until equality can be established from persisted data, the release tag must remain hidden. No further scope question is needed from the recorded answers.

### 2. Approaches message

**I recommend assessing and reusing the existing paths, changing only demonstrated gaps.** The distinguishing axis is whether provenance remains in its existing owners or moves behind a new shared read-time boundary.

The dependency checks available here are limited to the supplied fixtures: `svc-a/run-store.md` states the revision-match rule but does not expose its comparison fields; no executable implementations or test files were supplied to verify the selectors or rendered output. Those checks remain unverified. No live lookup was performed.

**Approach A — Reuse existing selectors and presentation paths.** Assess each surface against its documented provenance rule, including same-run date/version pairing, deterministic ordering, placement isolation, descendant touches, missing-version fallback, and release-tag eligibility. Reuse the shared hover renderer for the file tooltip. Add implementation changes only where that assessment finds a mismatch.

This preserves all approved behavior with the smallest blast radius. Its trade-off is that separate owners must continue to enforce consistent formatting and fallback rules.

Removes: none.  
Adds: focused verification coverage; only evidenced changes to existing selectors, completion persistence, or renderers—no new provenance construct.  
Pattern: follows the existing shared hover renderer in `svc-a/file-chip.md` and persisted metadata ownership in `svc-a/run-store.md`, while retaining the distinct provenance scopes in `svc-a/workspace.md`.

**Approach B — Introduce a shared read-time provenance resolver.** Give the three surfaces one resolver with explicit workspace, placement, and root scopes. It would reuse existing joins and return persisted date/version information, while leaving successful-completion persistence with the run store.

This centralizes ordering, missing-version handling, and release-tag eligibility, but introduces a new boundary and migrates three consumers despite no demonstrated inconsistency. It must not collapse their distinct provenance scopes.

Removes: surface-local provenance-selection orchestration that the resolver actually replaces; retain existing joins and the shared hover renderer.  
Adds: a scoped resolver contract and implementation, three consumer integrations, and resolver/integration tests.  
Pattern: preserves persisted-only rendering from `svc-b/response-contract.md`, but adds an abstraction over the existing owners described in `svc-a/workspace.md`.

Dropping the paired-deployment assumption is necessary in either approach; it does not justify dropping the approved release-tag feature. A workspace-only indicator is not viable because it would remove two explicitly retained surfaces.

I would switch to Approach B only if implementation inspection demonstrates duplicated or inconsistent selection logic that the existing shared paths cannot cleanly own.
